name: Auberge Saint-Antoine
insider_take: This isn't just a hotel—it's a living archaeological museum where 400-year-old artifacts are displayed behind glass floors and ancient stone walls form part of your room's décor.
whats_special: Built directly on the ruins of a 17th-century wharf and battery, Auberge Saint-Antoine showcases over 700 artifacts discovered during construction. Each room features original stone walls, maritime antiques, and some even have glass-enclosed archaeological displays. The hotel sits in Old Quebec's UNESCO World Heritage district, making it one of the few places where you can literally sleep among centuries of history.
pro_tip: Request a harbor-view room on the upper floors for stunning vistas of the St. Lawrence River and the hotel's rooftop urban garden where they grow herbs for their acclaimed restaurant.
dont_miss: The hotel's museum-quality artifact collection throughout the property, including cannonballs and ship remnants in the lobby. Take the complimentary archaeological tour to learn how this Relais & Châteaux property seamlessly blends luxury with Quebec City's colonial maritime heritage.
pros: Historic boutique hotel with authentic 17th-century architecture and archaeological artifacts
Prime location in Old Quebec's Lower Town near cobblestone streets and attractions
Award-winning Chez Muffy restaurant featuring farm-to-table Quebec cuisine
Luxurious spa services and elegantly appointed rooms with period furnishings
cons: Premium pricing reflects luxury positioning and historic setting
Limited parking availability due to Old Town location
